causes.text: On Aug. 28, 2025, Nvidia reported quarterly results showing a 56% surge in revenue and offered an upbeat forecast that affirmed booming demand for artificial-intelligence chips. The company's strong numbers reinforced confidence that corporate spending on AI infrastructure would remain elevated, encouraging investors to rotate into companies poised to benefit from the AI boom.

source_info.title: Snowflake shares surge as AI boom fuels demand for data platforms

causes.text: On Aug. 19, 2025, Databricks revealed that a planned Series K funding round would boost its valuation by about 61% to more than $100 billion. The announcement highlighted investors' willingness to commit billions to AI-native data platforms and implied that the addressable market for AI data infrastructure was large enough to support multiple high-value companies.

source_info.title: Databricks eyes over $100 billion valuation as investors back AI growth plans

effects.text: On Aug. 28, 2025, Snowflake's stock price jumped about 19%, adding more than $12.5 billion to its market value. Analysts said the surge reflected investor optimism that AI-driven demand would accelerate data-platform adoption and that high valuations for private AI companies signaled strong prospects for publicly traded peers.

source_info.title: Snowflake shares surge as AI boom fuels demand for data platforms

causal_reasoning_chain.description: Nvidia's blockbuster earnings report revealed a 56% jump in revenue and a bullish outlook for AI chips, reinforcing expectations that spending on artificial-intelligence infrastructure would remain strong. This prompted investors to reassess the earnings potential of companies that provide the software and data infrastructure underpinning AI applications.

Shortly beforehand, Databricks announced plans to raise capital at a valuation exceeding $100 billion, underscoring that venture investors were willing to assign sky-high valuations to AI-native data-platform providers. The financing signaled that the AI data-infrastructure market could support multiple large players and fueled expectations of robust growth across the sector.

By Aug. 28, investors connected the dots: strong chip demand and a lofty private-company valuation suggested that the AI data-infrastructure boom had momentum. Capital flowed into Snowflake, propelling its shares about 19% higher in a single day. The rally added more than $12.5 billion to its market capitalisation.

rationale: Two external signals—Nvidia's strong results and Databricks' high valuation—supported investor optimism about AI-driven data infrastructure. Together, they increased risk appetite for Snowflake as a potential beneficiary of the sector's growth.
counterfactual_analysis: If Nvidia's earnings had disappointed or Databricks' valuation had been muted, investor optimism about AI infrastructure might have been restrained. In that case, Snowflake's shares likely would not have surged 19%, even if the company's own fundamentals were strong.

adversarial_confounders.text: Snowflake itself raised its product revenue forecast around the same time.
adversarial_confounders.impact: The company's own guidance upgrade may have amplified the stock's reaction, making it harder to isolate the effect of external AI-related news.

details.commentary: Nvidia's strong results and Databricks' high valuation signaled investor demand across the AI infrastructure and data-platform ecosystem. Those signals suggested that Snowflake would face competition in an expanding market while retaining an opportunity for growth.

Positive news about AI chips and the valuation of a private data-platform company encouraged capital to flow into the sector. Investors' increased expectations for AI data infrastructure contributed to Snowflake's nearly twenty percent stock-price rise, reinforcing enthusiasm for potential beneficiaries of AI adoption.
